notes: GPUI PANEL. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React. You have no training knowledge of this exact API, so read before writing: rever/src/main.rs (the app shell: how views, listeners, hover, scrolling, text fields and theme are used here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src (theme tokens, icons, strings via `Lang::t`, the TextInput entity, preview::run), vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs (uniform_list.rs, scrollable.rs, input.rs) and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs for exact method names. What to build: the two zustand stores as plain structs with methods (same persistence keys and JSON shapes; persistence behind a small trait you define here with get/set of a string by key and an in-memory implementation, since the shared storage crate is being written by someone else right now), and two view structs implementing gpui::Render that reproduce the React components' layout, sizes, colors and behaviors (search, grouping by day, clear, remove; the bookmark bar with its overflow and remove). Navigation requests (clicking an entry opens it) are emitted as a GPUI event (`cx.emit` with an EventEmitter impl) carrying the URL, for the host to handle. Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css tokens (in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; if a token is missing, define it locally and list it in your report). All user-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the same keys the TSX uses. Keep logic in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; a .tsx gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-history --example preview_history` shows both views with realistic fixture data (use rever_ui_kit::preview::run). Look at your own work: while it runs, `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_history /tmp/preview_history.png` captures only that window; read the PNG, compare with what the TSX would render, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, and do not run the `rever` app. The first build of a GPUI crate takes a few minutes.
